findings.text: The receipts paragraph cites waverun/final/figure.log for the figure render and overlap check, and that path does not exist under the run directory; the render log that does exist is waverun/final-titan/figure.log (REVISION=7b9c467e4, OVERLAP_CHECK=clean, PNG written to waverun/per-slice-wall.png). The fact it asserts is true and the receipt a reader is told to open is not there, so the render check cannot be verified from the fragment alone. The figure itself does regenerate byte-identically (21464 bytes, differing only in dc:date and matplotlib element ids) from waverun/h200-stage.log through scripts/prototypes/bank_step_batch/plot.py, whose overlap check passes.

The artifacts line presents waverun/head/gate.log and waverun/head/negative.log as 'same arms re-run at the head 299841a4c', but when the record was written only waverun/head/gate.log existed and it held two header lines and no EXIT= line, while waverun/head/negative.log did not exist at all. Both arms have since completed at that revision and are correct (gate: 2 passed in 823.97s, EXIT=0; control: 1 failed, 1 passed, EXIT=1 with the lane-broadcast AssertionError at tests/test_bank_step_batch.py:164), so the statement has become true after the fact rather than having been recorded when it was made. A record that declares work complete on arms still running cannot be told apart from one whose arms failed, until someone re-reads the logs.

stage_walls gives its WALL and STAGE branches identical bodies (both assign item['per_slice_ms'] into the same dict by (name, slices)), so the two-branch test carries no distinction and one branch would express the same behaviour.
